title: An algebraic index-one DVR extension with perfect residue field
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ of characteristic $p>0$. There is an algebraic field extension $P/K$ [def-pc-field-extension] such that the integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in $P$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a discrete valuation ring, $\mathfrak m_AA'=\mathfrak m_{A'}$, and $A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$ is perfect and purely inseparable algebraic over $k$. Algebraic means that each element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the base; purely inseparable means that some $p$-power of each element lies in the base; perfect means that every element has a $p$th root. The field $P$ is a directed union of finite subextensions $P_j/K$ whose integral closures $A_j$ are discrete valuation rings with $\mathfrak m_AA_j=\mathfrak m_{A_j}$, and $A'=\bigcup_j A_j$. No completeness, finite $p$-basis, or characteristic assumption on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof paragraph constructing A' by adjoining all p-power roots of lifts of a residue p-base, lines 35980–35993.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists], choose a $p$-basis $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ of $k$ and lifts $x_i\in A$. The characteristic of the field $k$ makes $p$ prime. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. For every $i$, recursively choose $\alpha_{i,0}=x_i$ and $\alpha_{i,n+1}\in\Omega$ with $\alpha_{i,n+1}^p=\alpha_{i,n}$; the defining root property in [def-weil-algebraic-closure] applies to the monic polynomial $T^p-\alpha_{i,n}$. Thus $\alpha_{i,n}^{p^n}=x_i$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: choice of lifts of a residue p-base; compatible roots made explicit

proof.text: For finite $J\subseteq I$ and $n\geq1$ form $B_{J,n}=A[T_i:i\in J]/(T_i^{p^n}-x_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] successively, in any ordering of $J$. It gives the finite free basis $\prod_{i\in J}T_i^{e_i}$, $0\leq e_i<p^n$, and reduction $B_{J,n}/\pi B_{J,n}=k[T_i:i\in J]/(T_i^{p^n}-b_i)$. Every finite subfamily of the p-basis is p-independent. By [lem-sfb-p-independent-root-quotient-field], this reduction is a field and every element of it has its $p^n$th power in $k$. The empty $J$ gives $B_{\varnothing,n}=A$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: finite subsets of the displayed root presentation and their closed fibres

proof.text: The basis in Step 2 has positive finite cardinality $p^{n|J|}$. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-free-field-fibre-dvr] therefore hold, so $B_{J,n}$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$ and injective map from $A$. Evaluation $T_i\mapsto\alpha_{i,n}$ defines an $A$-algebra map $B_{J,n}\to\Omega$. It is injective: by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] a nonzero element is $u\pi^a$, whose image is nonzero since a unital map sends a unit to a unit and $\pi\ne0$ in $K\subseteq\Omega$. Identify $B_{J,n}$ with this image.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: the finite algebras are DVR extensions, with their realization in one field

proof.text: If $J\subseteq J_1$ and $n\leq m$, the formula $\alpha_{i,n}=\alpha_{i,m}^{p^{m-n}}$ gives $B_{J,n}\subseteq B_{J_1,m}$. These inclusions preserve units and $\pi$ is a nonunit in both DVRs. Writing a nonzero element as $u\pi^a$ shows that it belongs to $\pi B_{J_1,m}$ exactly when $a>0$, hence exactly when it belongs to $\pi B_{J,n}$. Thus the inclusions are local and induce injective residue-field maps. The pairs $(J,n)$ are directed by $(J\cup J_1,\max(n,m))$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: injective compatible transitions and index one

proof.text: Put $A^*=\bigcup_{J,n}B_{J,n}$ inside $\Omega$ and $P_{J,n}=\operatorname{Frac}(B_{J,n})$. A nonzero denominator in a finite stage is $u\pi^a$, so $P_{J,n}=B_{J,n}[1/\pi]$. Its monomial basis from Step 2 spans it over $K=A[1/\pi]$, hence $P_{J,n}/K$ is finite. Set $P=\bigcup_{J,n}P_{J,n}$; directedness makes this a field, algebraic over $K$, and $P=\operatorname{Frac}(A^*)$. Every nonzero element of $A^*$ has the form $u\pi^a$ with $u\in(A^*)^\times$. Also $\pi$ is not invertible in $A^*$, since an inverse would lie at a finite stage, contradicting Step 4. Hence $A^*$ is local with nonunits precisely $\pi A^*$. For a nonzero ideal $H\subseteq A^*$, choose the least exponent $a$ occurring among its nonzero elements. A corresponding $u\pi^a\in H$ gives $\pi^a\in H$, and all elements of $H$ are divisible by $\pi^a$, so $H=\pi^aA^*$. The domain $A^*$ is therefore a DVR by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and $\mathfrak m_AA^*=\pi A^*=\mathfrak m_{A^*}$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: directed union is a DVR; explicit ideal argument instead of assuming filtered unions are Noetherian

proof.text: Each $B_{J,n}$ is integral over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and Step 2. Since it is a PID, [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes it integrally closed in $P_{J,n}$. An element of $P_{J,n}$ integral over $A$ satisfies the same monic equation over $B_{J,n}$, so lies in $B_{J,n}$. Thus $B_{J,n}$ is exactly the integral closure $A_j$ specified in the statement. Similarly $A^*$ is integral over $A$ element by element and is integrally closed in $P$ by the same PID theorem. Every element of $P$ integral over $A$ is then in $A^*$, so the requested integral closure $A^{\prime}$ equals $A^*$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation: identification with the integral closures, both finite and infinite

proof.text: Step 4 identifies $k^*=A^*/\pi A^*$ with the union of the finite-stage residue fields: surjectivity is representation at a finite stage, and if an element of one stage equals $\pi y$ in the union, put it and $y$ in a common later stage and use the contraction calculation. Each residue $z$ lies in some $B_{J,n}/\pi$ and has $z^{p^n}\in k$ by Step 2, proving pure inseparability and algebraicity. To prove perfection, first let $a\in k$. The p-basis expansion is $a=\sum_E c_E^p b^E$ with finitely many terms and $c_E\in k$. In $k^*$ the element $\sum_E c_E\prod_i\bar\alpha_{i,1}^{E_i}$ has pth power $a$. Every element of $k^*$ is a finite $k$-linear combination of monomials in the $\bar\alpha_{i,n}$ by Step 2. Choose pth roots of its finitely many coefficients by the preceding formula and replace each $\bar\alpha_{i,n}$ by $\bar\alpha_{i,n+1}$; the resulting finite sum has pth power the original element, since Frobenius preserves sums and products in characteristic $p$. All terms belong to one common finite stage. Thus $k^*$ is perfect. Together with Steps 5–6 this proves every clause, without assuming $I$ finite or completing $A$.
